systems.summary: A design by The 3DO Company that other firms built and sold: Panasonic first, then GoldStar, Sanyo and Creative. An ARM60 runs it.
Developed by Nintendo's research and engineering team and built by Nintendo and Foxconn. Two ARM processors and a DMP PICA200 graphics chip run it.

Atari's subsidiary Cyan Engineering built the prototype, codenamed Stella, after Nolan Bushnell went looking for a programmable home console. A MOS 6507 processor and the Television Interface Adaptor (TIA) run it.

people.name: Nolan Bushnell
people.role: Atari's CEO, who wanted a programmable home console

systems.summary: Designed for Atari by General Computer Corporation; its MARIA chip draws arcade-style graphics, and it plays almost all 2600 cartridges.
Atari's last console, built for it by IBM. Two custom chips, Tom and Jerry, do the graphics and sound beside a Motorola 68000.
Atari's colour handheld, developed at Epyx by Dave Needle and RJ Mical, two of the Amiga's designers.
Coleco's console, built around a Zilog Z80, a TMS9928A video chip and an SN76489 sound chip.
Developed by a team under Hideki Sato, with a Hitachi SH-4, NEC's PowerVR2 graphics and a Yamaha sound chip. Sega's NAOMI arcade board is based on it.

people.name: Hideki Sato
people.role: Led the team that developed it

systems.summary: Nintendo's disk drive for the Famicom; its Ricoh 2C33 adds a wavetable sound channel.
Developed and made by Nintendo, with Foxconn also building it. IBM made its Gekko processor and ATI its Flipper graphics chip; the Triforce arcade board is based on it.
Sega's colour handheld, built around a Zilog Z80 and the Texas Instruments sound chip of the Master System. The Genesis Nomad came after it.
Nintendo R&D1 designed it under Gunpei Yokoi and Satoru Okada. Its Sharp SM83 processor carried on in the Game Boy Color and, for the older games, in the Game Boy Advance.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.role: Led the design team at Nintendo R&D1

people.name: Satoru Okada
people.role: Led the design with Yokoi; developed the Game Link Cable

systems.summary: Built by Nintendo's research and engineering team around an ARM7TDMI. The Game Boy's Sharp SM83 sits beside it, so the older cartridges still play.
The Game Boy in colour, from Nintendo's research and engineering team. It keeps the Game Boy's Sharp SM83 processor and plays its cartridges.
Mattel's console, run on a General Instrument CP1600; INTV Corporation took it over in 1984.
Sega's third-generation console, made by Sega and by Tectoy. A Zilog Z80 runs it; its Texas Instruments sound chip is the one of the SG-1000 and the Game Gear.
Designed by a Sega team under Hideki Sato and Masami Ishikawa. A Motorola 68000 and a Zilog Z80 run it; the sound comes from a Yamaha YM2612 and the SN76489 of the Master System.
Nintendo developed it with Silicon Graphics. NEC made its VR4300 processor and the Reality Coprocessor (RCP), which draws the picture.
Developed by Nintendo and built by Foxconn, with two ARM processors: an ARM946E-S, and the Game Boy Advance's ARM7TDMI.
The Neo Geo on CD-ROM instead of cartridges, with the same Motorola 68000 as the cartridge console.
SNK's home console with the same hardware as its MVS arcade board: a Motorola 68000 runs the games, a Z80 the sound.
Designed by Masayuki Uemura, first as the Famicom, and developed by Nintendo R&D2. Ricoh made its 2A03 processor and the 2C02 picture chip.
SNK's colour handheld: a Toshiba TLCS-900/H runs the games and a Z80 the sound.
Made by NEC with Hudson Soft. The processor is Hudson Soft's HuC6280, the picture chips its HuC6270 and HuC6260.
Made by Nintendo with The Pokémon Company. A small Seiko Epson S1C88 processor runs the games.
The PlayStation's successor, from Sony Computer Entertainment. Its Emotion Engine processor was developed with Toshiba; the Graphics Synthesizer draws the picture.
A handheld from Sony Computer Entertainment, with a processor based on the MIPS R4000. It came in several models, among them the PSP Go.

best_selling.title: Grand Theft Auto: Liberty City Stories

systems.summary: Designed mainly by Ken Kutaragi and Sony Computer Entertainment in Japan, around an R3000 processor designed by MIPS Technologies. The PS one model followed.
Sega's fifth-generation console, with two Hitachi SH-2 processors, two picture processors (VDP1 and VDP2) and a Yamaha sound chip.
Sega's add-on for the Mega Drive, with two SH-2 processors of its own; it was meant to carry players over to the Saturn.
Sega's CD-ROM add-on for the Mega Drive. Its own Motorola 68000, faster than the Mega Drive's, runs the CD side, a custom ASIC scales and rotates graphics, and a Ricoh chip handles the sound.
Made on the advice of Hayao Nakayama, then head of Sega in Japan. Texas Instruments made its picture and sound chips; the sound chip returned in the Master System and the Game Gear.

people.name: Hayao Nakayama
people.role: Head of Sega in Japan; it was made on his advice

systems.summary: Designed by Masayuki Uemura and developed by Nintendo R&D2. Ricoh made its 5A22 processor and the picture chips; the sound runs on Nintendo's S-SMP.

best_selling.title: Street Fighter II: The World Warrior

systems.summary: Made by NEC Home Electronics. It has the PC Engine's HuC6280A processor, with two HuC6270 picture chips and a HuC6202 to blend them.

chips.name: Hudson Soft HuC6270 (VDC), two of them

systems.summary: Conceived by John Ross at Smith Engineering as a handheld; it became a tabletop console with its own vector screen.
Made at Nintendo R&D1 under Gunpei Yokoi; an NEC V810 drives its red 3D display.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.role: Led its development as general manager of Nintendo R&D1

systems.summary: Shigeru Miyamoto and Genyo Takeda led its development. IBM made the Broadway processor; the graphics chip is ATI's Hollywood.

people.name: Shigeru Miyamoto
people.role: Led its development, with Genyo Takeda

people.name: Genyo Takeda
people.role: Led its development, with Shigeru Miyamoto

systems.summary: Bandai's handheld, developed with Gunpei Yokoi's company Koto Laboratory; it was the last hardware he worked on. An NEC V30 MZ runs it.

people.name: Gunpei Yokoi
people.role: Developed it with Bandai through his company, Koto Laboratory; his last hardware

systems.summary: Microsoft's first console, built from PC parts. Flextronics and Wistron made it; an Intel Pentium III processor and an Nvidia NV2A graphics chip sit inside.
